Definition: a stumbling-block, literally or figuratively (obstacle, enticement (specifically an idol), scruple)
BiblicalUsage: A stumbling block is anything set in the path that makes a person fall, and Scripture uses it both literally and for sin itself. The law forbids putting one before the blind, Isaiah calls the LORD Himself a stone of stumbling to those who refuse Him, and Ezekiel names the idols in the heart as the stumbling block of iniquity.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word is a warning in both directions: I must not set a trap in another person's path, and I must not let my own heart keep the idol that trips me. Christ is the stone the builders rejected, and He is either the foundation or the fall.
